findings.claim: The ledger write at line 771-772 records the fetch_head-derived `policy_sha` before `reverify()` (line 776) has run, so if `reverify` raises `PackageError` for an errored gate (line 528, an infrastructure fault that per the gate contract must never be charged to the task and aborts the attempt), the ledger has already committed a claim that this task's re-verification ran under that declaration when it never actually completed. On retry the value self-corrects only if the newly computed policy_sha happens to differ again from the stale one; in the meantime the row asserts a declaration for a verification that errored out, which is the exact 'ran under' claim `record_policy`'s own docstring (ledger.py:497-500) says should only be issued for a completed re-verification. No test exercises this path — every test double for `reverify` returns cleanly — so the mismatch only shows up in production when a repo's gate toolchain is briefly broken at `fetch_head`, not in fixtures.

This test is the witness for acceptance criterion 4 in `.saffron/specs/SA-0046-a-task-cannot-say-which-policy-it-ran-under.md` (line 49), which names it literally as `tests/test_package.py::test_reverifying_under_an_unchanged_policy_does_not_touch_the_row`. The spec's frontmatter is `forbidden` here, so that witness string is fixed, but the test actually written is named `test_reverifying_under_an_unchanged_policy_issues_no_policy_write`. `saffron/gates/core/criteria.py`'s `_judge` matches a criterion's witness against collected pytest node ids by exact string membership, so the declared witness for the spec's own most-emphasized criterion ("the fourth witness is the one to write first") does not exist at head, and criterion 4 has no test satisfying its literal contract even though an equivalent-looking test exists under a different name.
